business: ArmorHub, a marketplace that sends customers to verified service partners and sellers (partner side)
by_behaviour: Gets customers by word of mouth and Instagram
Worried customers will bypass the platform
why_not: Joining is free, so I might look at it, but I do not want to quote blind against my competitors on price, and I do not trust a platform that takes 10% off every job when my customers could simply take my number and go direct next time.

I would sign up because it is free, but I will not pay a 10% cut on jobs until I see real requests coming in. I have no idea how many jobs per month this brings to a shop like mine, and I cannot plan my staff or my cash on a promise.

Customers sending jobs is useful on paper, but the upfront ID, commercial registration and approval wait is exactly the paperwork I avoid. I get paid on the day, and a 10% cut on every job plus waiting for a reviewer is a cost I have to see before I'd even try it.

I like the idea of customers coming to me and the money being held until the job is done, but I do not want to upload my ID and commercial registration and then wait for someone to approve me before I can even quote. I have enough paperwork already and I would rather keep working the way I do now.

I run a real service centre with staff to pay, and my margin on a PPF or tint job is already thin. Taking 10% of every order before I even see the money is a lot, and I have no way of knowing yet whether these customers are worth it.

I run an established centre with staff and my own customers, and a 10% cut on every job plus quoting blind against other shops on price cuts into what I keep by dealing direct. The held payment would help with unpaid jobs, but it does not bring me anything I cannot already get.
I already get my work from Instagram and WhatsApp, and it covers my bookings without any extra steps. I do not see why I would add another channel and a commission on top of that.
My shop already gets steady work from Instagram and WhatsApp and from people who know us. I don't see why I'd pay 10% of every job to a new app when my current channels work.

I take most of my work through WhatsApp and Instagram and keep all of it. A platform that takes 10% of every paid job is taking money from my own customers, and I don't want a middleman between me and the people who already know my number.
why_yes: Slow months hurt me and I need jobs coming in, so I would join since it is free and only costs me when I get paid. I still want to see the work before I trust it.
I am always hungry for new customers and slow months hurt. Joining costs nothing, so I would test it on a few jobs before deciding anything bigger.

Customers paying into escrow and getting a written warranty automatically is the part that makes me willing to try it, since I already get most of my bookings from WhatsApp and Instagram and do not want to chase payments. I would test it on one or two jobs before committing more.

Joining is free and I am short of jobs in slow months, so I would sign up and try a couple of quotes. But I still have to see whether the customers are real and whether the money gets paid out to me, because I do not hand my bookings to anyone without proof.

Joining costs nothing and slow months hurt, so I would sign up and try one job to see if the customers are real. But 10% off every order is a big bite out of a tint or film job that already has thin margins.

Joining is free and the money stays held until the job is done, which covers the unpaid-jobs problem that keeps me up at night. I would try it on a couple of jobs to see whether the requests are real, but I would not move my Instagram and WhatsApp work onto it.
flip: A lower commission on the first few orders, or a clear record showing these leads close often enough that the 10% pays for itself.
Proof that the app sends paying jobs in my area that I could not get on my own, with customers who stay on the platform.
Seeing real paying customers in Riyadh or Cairo asking for jobs I can do, before I have to upload any papers.
If ArmorHub showed me that most of the jobs it sends are new customers I could not get on my own, and that repeat customers are blocked from bypassing the platform, I would test it on a few jobs.
Verified customers who are clearly ready to book, with a real track record of finished jobs and no monthly cost, at a level that clearly brings in work I wouldn't get otherwise.
Starting to quote and get paid right away, with the approval and document upload handled after my first job, or a clear per-job fee with no document step.
Being able to quote and see the requests straight away without uploading documents or waiting for approval, with the first customers already in the inbox.
Seeing proof from shops like mine in Riyadh or Cairo: a real count of requests and booked jobs per month in my area, and a clear view of who the customers are before I commit.
If approval were quick and I could see a few real nearby requests with the money held safely before I had to upload anything.
Customers I cannot reach any other way, at a commission lower than what I spend to win them myself, with no price-only bidding.
Seeing a real monthly count of paid, completed jobs from sellers in Riyadh or Cairo who do what I do, plus a few real requests shown to me before I have to commit anything.
Seeing real jobs from businesses like mine in Riyadh or Cairo, with the price visible and the money actually paid out to a seller on time.
